Doctor: Have you experienced any hematuria, nausea, vomiting, or fever associated with the pain? Patient: I did notice some blood in my urine this morning, and I've been feeling pretty nauseous. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior episodes of kidney stones or similar symptoms in the past? Patient: Yes, I've had kidney stones before—this might be my third time. Doctor: Have you experienced any fever during this current episode, and if so, what was the highest temperature recorded? Additionally, have you had any prior surgical interventions for kidney stones or related complications? Patient: I haven't had a fever, but I did have some chills. I don't remember having any surgery for kidney stones before. Doctor: Could you describe the location of the pain, whether it radiates to any other areas, and if you have any other symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or blood in your urine? Patient: The pain started on my left back and has been traveling lower, but it's still mostly on the left side. I haven't passed the stone yet, and I've had some blood in my urine this morning. I also feel really nauseous and can't eat because of the pain. It's been constant and really intense. Doctor: Have you had any recent imaging studies
